transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about my face. The left side looks crooked to me, messed up, and I feel like people at the warehouse—or even when I go salsa dancing—are noticing it. They say they don’t see anything, but… I don’t really believe it.
Is this concern about your face affecting your daily life or activities in any way?

Yeah… it has. I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get behind, like I’m delayed checking myself or trying not to be seen. And I’ve stopped going to soccer and salsa nights a lot… family stuff too, especially if there might be pictures. I just don’t want people looking at me.
Do you think your face is actually crooked, or is it just that you feel like it looks that way to others?
I… I think it is crooked. Or at least it looks that way to me. The left side just looks messed up, and I can’t stop noticing it. Even when people say they don’t see it, I still feel like they do.
Do you think other people can see that your face is crooked, even if they say they don't notice anything?
Yeah… I do. I mean, they say they don’t notice anything, but I feel like they can see the left side looks crooked. Like at work or salsa night, I just assume people are noticing it.
Do you think it's possible that your face might actually look normal, and it's just your own perception that it's crooked?

I guess… maybe it’s possible. But it doesn’t feel that way to me. I can’t stop seeing the left side looking crooked, messed up, and I keep thinking people at the warehouse or at salsa night notice it even if they say they don’t.
Do you think your belief about your face being crooked is based on something you see, or is it more of a feeling you have?

It’s… both, I guess. I see it when I look at myself—the left side just looks crooked and messed up. But then it turns into this feeling that everyone at the warehouse or at salsa is noticing it too, even when they say they don’t.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about your face being crooked is false, or are you absolutely certain it's true?

I mean… I know people say they don’t see anything, so maybe there’s a chance I’m wrong. But it doesn’t feel false to me. I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked, and that people at work or salsa notice it.
Do you think anyone could convince you that your face is not actually crooked?

I don’t know. People tell me they don’t see anything, but… I still can’t stop seeing the left side of my face as crooked. It’s hard to believe them, especially when I’m at the warehouse or salsa night and I feel like everyone’s noticing.
Do you think your belief about your face being crooked is something that might be true even if no one else can see it?

Yeah… I guess that’s what scares me. Like, even if they say they don’t see it, I still see the left side looking crooked and messed up. So part of me thinks maybe it’s there and they’re just not noticing… or not saying it. At work, or at salsa, it feels like people can tell.
Do you think your belief about your face being crooked would change if a doctor or a plastic surgeon told you that there's nothing wrong with your face?

Maybe for a little bit… I don’t know. If a doctor said it, I’d try to believe it. But I think I’d still keep seeing the left side of my face as crooked, and I’d still worry people at the warehouse or salsa night notice it.
Do you think your belief about your face being crooked is a delusion?
I… I don’t really know what counts as that. It feels real to me, but I guess I can’t say for sure.
Do you think there's any part of you that recognizes your belief about your face being crooked might not be based in reality?

A little, maybe. I mean… I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about the left side of my face looking crooked. People say they don’t see it, but when I’m at the warehouse or at salsa night, it feels like they notice. So… I don’t know. Part of me wonders if I’m seeing it wrong, but it still feels real.
Would you say your belief about your face being crooked is something that could never be proven wrong to you, no matter what anyone else says or shows you?

I don’t know if I’d say never. I mean… if someone showed me, maybe I’d try to take it in. But I’m here because I can’t stop seeing the left side of my face as crooked and messed up, and it feels like people at work or salsa notice it, even when they say they don’t.
Do you think there is any evidence that could completely change your mind about your face being crooked?

I’m not sure. Maybe if I could really believe what people tell me, that they don’t see anything… but I still keep seeing the left side of my face as crooked. At work, or at salsa, it just feels like everyone notices, even when they say they don’t.
Do you think you might be misinterpreting how others perceive your face?

Maybe. I mean… I know people tell me they don’t see anything. But I keep thinking the left side of my face looks crooked, and when I’m at the warehouse or salsa night it feels like they’re noticing it. I can’t really shake that.
Do you think your face is crooked even if a mirror or a photo shows it's not?

Yeah… even if a photo looks okay, I still end up focusing on the left side. It just looks crooked to me. I can’t stop thinking people at the warehouse or salsa notice it, even when they say they don’t.
Do you think your face could look perfectly normal to everyone else, but still be crooked to you?
Yeah… I guess that’s possible. Like, other people might think I look normal, but to me the left side still looks crooked and messed up. I can’t stop seeing it.
Do you think your face is crooked regardless of what anyone else tells you or what evidence you might see?
Yeah… pretty much. Even when people say they don’t see it, or something looks okay, I still feel like the left side of my face is crooked. I keep thinking people at work or salsa can notice it.
Do you think there is anything that could ever change your belief about your face being crooked?

I don’t know… maybe if I could stop seeing it that way. But right now, even when people say they don’t notice anything, I still keep thinking the left side of my face looks crooked. It’s hard to believe anything else.
